facts.fact: The Department of State Services is prosecuting activist and presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore under the Cybercrimes Act for describing President Tinubu as a criminal, and its Director-General announced on 30 August 2026 that the prosecution would be suspended until after the 2027 election; the charge date is not given.
facts.system: Prosecution of Omoyele Sowore under the Cybercrimes Act

facts.fact: SERAP, a Nigerian rights group, and Sowore's lawyer Adeyinka Olumide-Fusika publicly demanded on 31 August 2026 that the DSS withdraw its charges against Sowore, calling the prosecution an unacceptable use of criminal law against a critic.

note: The 2022 ECOWAS Court judgment on section 24 of the Cybercrimes Act is a regional ruling with no stated government action, so no repealed fact.
